limits: Covers the MODULE's refusals, not any caller's use of them - nothing sources scripts/gate-lib.sh yet, and #1061's constraint 1 is why this control lands first. Each case's probe.sh is run under sh AND bash and the two are required to agree, because the idiom this module replaces does not: '${2:?}' exits 1 under bash and 2 under dash, so scripts/shellcheck-gate.sh - which declares exit 1 = findings - reports a usage error as a finding under one shell and as UNKNOWN under the other. A single-shell control cannot see that, which is why the disagreement is its own verdict here rather than folded into either answer. detect_signal keys on the runner's 'refused' line rather than on the exit status because a probe that CRASHES also exits non-zero (#946): the runner requires the module to have SAID 'gate-lib: refused - ' in the probe's own output, and a crash without it lands in unknown/exit 2, which is crash-distinct rather than 'detected'. NOT covered: whether a migrated gate actually routes through the module - that is #1127's question and needs that gate's own control, not this one.

anchors.origin: the 'substitute a sensible default' module design refuted by #1061 constraint 2
anchors.note: No historical commit exists because this module has no pre-fix version - the control is required to land BEFORE any caller. What is vendored is therefore the DESIGN this module rejects, with the same --check runner so a verdict difference isolates the four library functions and nothing else. Provenance reads 'unverified' for that structural reason rather than a temporary one: there is nothing in git history for --verify-provenance to resolve, and there never will be.

mutations.name: one-good-exit
mutations.protection: two verdicts may not both map to the good exit 0 (bad-unknown-maps-to-good)

mutations.name: last-argument-flag
mutations.protection: a flag that is the last argument has no value and is refused (bad-final-flag)

mutations.name: map-required
mutations.protection: emitting or exiting before gate_map is refused (bad-no-map)
mutations.why: MASKED, by design, and honest rather than a false green (the single-mutation limitation re-dispositioned under #1268 R3). With the map requirement disabled, bad-no-map still reaches gate_exit, whose own lookup finds no code for the verdict in an empty map and refuses it - so the case is refused through a second protection and this one reads UNCAUGHT. Each protection covers for the other; a case isolating this one would need a probe that emits and never exits, which is not a state any gate is allowed to reach.

mutations.name: unmapped-verdict
mutations.protection: a verdict the map never declared is refused, never given a code (bad-unmapped-verdict)
